summary: Echoes from the Dust is an interactive 3D web museum designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the historic spacecraft, rovers, and landers NASA has left across the Moon and Mars. By transforming planetary coordinates into a navigable celestial globe with first-person machine diaries, the platform turns distant space hardware into accessible stories of scientific discovery.
details: The Problem & Vision Since the 1960s, NASA has left dozens of pioneering machines on the Moon, Mars, and deep space. To many young students, these deactivated landers and rovers seem like distant relics or forgotten hardware. Echoes from the Dust reframes these machines as enduring pioneers that unlocked humanity’s understanding of the solar system. ​How It Works Built as a lightweight, browser-based 3D interactive museum, the application allows students to: ​Explore Celestial Worlds in 3D: Users can freely rotate, zoom, and switch between high-resolution 3D globes of Mars and The Moon, rendered with authentic NASA planetary surface maps. ​Inspect Real Landing Coordinates: Glowing interactive beacons mark the exact latitude and longitude where historic missions touched down—including the Opportunity Rover at Endeavour Crater, Viking 1 at Chryse Planitia, the Apollo 11 Descent Stage in the Sea of Tranquility, and the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle at Hadley Rille. ​Read First-Person Machine Logs: Clicking any beacon opens an exhibit card featuring a first-person narrative written from the perspective of the hardware itself, making space history emotionally engaging and easy for K–12 students to grasp. ​Discover the Science Legacy: Each exhibit translates complex instrumentation into clear takeaways—explaining how Opportunity found evidence of ancient Martian water through hematite "blueberries," how Apollo 11’s laser retroreflectors are still used today to measure the Moon's distance, and how early landers paved the way for human exploration. ​Technical Stack & NASA Open Data ​Frontend & 3D Graphics: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js (WebGL) for real-time 3D spherical rendering, raycasting pin selection, and orbital camera controls. ​NASA Data & Resources: Utilizes NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Mars surface imagery, along with authentic mission landing coordinates and historical mission logs. ​Impact By combining interactive 3D visualization with empathetic storytelling, Echoes from the Dust requires zero installation and works on any classroom computer or mobile browser—inspiring the next generation of engineers, scientists, and space explorers.
